content_sections.heading: About BRIC-NIPGR
content_sections.text: The BRIC-National Institute of Plant Genome Research is based at Aruna Asaf Ali Marg, New Delhi. According to its letterhead, it is part of BRIC, a DBT organisation. These posts are in two Department of Biotechnology (DBT) projects on sheath blight disease in rice. The work is supervised by Dr. Gopaljee Jha, Scientist, BRIC-NIPGR.

content_sections.heading: BRIC-NIPGR Research Associate-I Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: A Ph.D. degree in Life Sciences/Biotechnology/Molecular Biology/Microbiology or a related field. You must also meet the guidelines in DST Office Memorandum No. DST/PCPM/Z-06/2022 dated June 26, 2023. Under the same DST office memorandum, candidates with an M.Tech in Biotechnology/Bioinformatics can also apply if they have three years of research experience and a relevant research publication. Preference goes to candidates with relevant experience in molecular biology, genome editing, handling transgenic plants, plant-pathogen handling, formulations and protein biochemistry. This experience should be backed by publications in SCI journals: at least one first-author paper or two co-author papers, each with an impact factor above 3. Check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of the post before you apply.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Applications are screened, and BRIC-NIPGR may raise the eligibility criteria for shortlisting if it receives many applications. Shortlisted candidates receive an email with the interview link and the date and time of the online interview. Ineligible candidates will not be shortlisted. BRIC-NIPGR will select candidates based on their qualifications and experience.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The positions are purely temporary and end when the projects end. The first appointment is for one year or until the project ends, whichever comes first. The tenure may be cut short based on the candidate's performance and at the discretion of the Competent Authority. Either side may end the appointment at any time by giving one month's notice. Appointees will have no claim, implicit or explicit, to any regular position at BRIC-NIPGR.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for BRIC-NIPGR Research Associate-I Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Before you apply, make sure you meet the essential qualification. Write a cover letter saying you are interested in the post. Prepare your complete biodata and self-attested soft copies of your marksheets and certificates from Class X onwards, plus proof of your research experience and publications. Combine the application form, cover letter and all documents into a single PDF file. Fill in the BRIC-NIPGR application Google Form in the given format and upload the PDF within 15 days of 23 October 2026. Only applications made through this Google Form are accepted. Applications that are incomplete, in the wrong format or sent any other way will be rejected, as will those without the supporting educational certificates. For questions, email the scientist in charge only, at [email protected] .

faq.question: Q1. Can I apply with an M.Tech instead of a Ph.D.?
faq.answer: Yes. You can apply with an M.Tech in Biotechnology/Bioinformatics if you also have three years of research experience and a relevant research publication, as allowed by DST OM No. DST/PCPM/Z-06/2022.

faq.question: Q2. What is the monthly salary?
faq.answer: Each Research Associate-I receives Rs. 58,000 per month plus 27% HRA, as sanctioned in the project.

faq.question: Q3. Which projects are these posts in?
faq.answer: There is one post in each of two DBT projects: one on antifungal peptide-based formulations to manage sheath blight in rice, and one on sheath blight tolerance in rice through genome editing of a susceptibility factor.

faq.question: Q4. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: Applications must be submitted within 15 days of the advertisement dated 23 October 2026, which works out to 7 November 2026.

faq.question: Q5. What publications improve my chances?
faq.answer: Candidates with at least one first-author paper or two co-author papers in SCI journals with an impact factor above 3 will be preferred.

faq.question: Q6. Which documents go into the PDF?
faq.answer: One PDF must contain the application form, a cover letter, your complete biodata, self-attested marksheets and certificates from Class X onwards, and proof of your research experience and publications.

faq.question: Q7. Is the interview in person?
faq.answer: No, the interview is online. Shortlisted candidates receive the link, date and time by email, and no TA/DA is paid.

faq.question: Q8. How long is the appointment?
faq.answer: The first appointment is for one year or until the project ends, whichever is earlier. Either side can end it with one month's notice.

faq.question: Q9. Whom do I contact with questions?
faq.answer: Email Dr. Gopaljee Jha, the scientist in charge, at [email protected]. Queries are accepted by email only.
